failure_patterns.pattern: endpoint_or_tool_identity_mismatch: Calls used an abbreviated or incorrectly formatted tool name, a neighboring operation, or a less suitable endpoint.

rejected_edits.content: - Deduplicate identical calls unless the user explicitly requests separate or repeated passes. Preserve separate invocations for separately requested passes—even when the endpoint and entity recur, such as an explicit repeat, a second sort, or a request for more items. For a “more” or “next page” request, use the next page or index only when the schema supports pagination and the wording establishes continuation; retain each pass’s requested filters or sorting. Do not infer repetition or pagination from narrative context alone. Do not add related calls as extra checks. An explicitly requested draw or simulation is its own outcome and requires the corresponding draw or simulation operation, not a related catalog or list endpoint.
rejected_edits.target: - Deduplicate the call set: make one invocation per distinct requested operation and input unless the schema supports batching or the user requests repetition. Do not add related calls as extra checks. An explicitly requested draw or simulation is its own outcome and requires the corresponding draw or simulation operation, not a related catalog or list endpoint.

rejected_edits.content: - For optional search-mode, entity-type, platform, category, or format selectors, use the documented choice matching a class, mode, platform, or format clearly identified by the requested result—even when expressed as a descriptor rather than as “filter by” (for example, “PC game giveaways”). Do not choose an arbitrary restrictive value for another selector dimension the user left unspecified; omit it, or use a documented all/any value only when needed to express the requested scope.
rejected_edits.target: - For optional search-mode or entity-type selectors, use the documented choice that matches an entity class or mode clearly identified in the request, even if the user did not phrase it as a filter. Do not choose an arbitrary restrictive value for another selector dimension the user left unspecified; omit it, or use a documented all/any value only when needed to express the requested scope.

rejected_edits.content: - Before responding, run a concise call-by-call, two-way audit: map every requested outcome to a fitting call and remove any call that serves none. Verify each call's operation, source, requested entity/property, and result granularity, and copy the exact tool identifier from the tool list. Check every argument against that endpoint's own schema and the request: exact field, grounded value with the documented type and canonical form, required-versus-optional placement exactly once, and every compatible explicit constraint. Encode values using the active format's required wire representation. Preserve supported counts, pages, and range bounds; omit unsupported or unrequested values, and never fabricate missing required inputs or use blank/null placeholders. In name/value-entry formats, emit one entry per parameter, never a packed object. Emit one invocation per object, then verify the complete response parses as valid JSON in the exact required wrapper and keys, including required empty arrays.
rejected_edits.target: - Before responding, perform a two-way audit: map every requested outcome to the call or calls that fulfill it, checking each endpoint's operation, source, and requested result granularity; then ensure every call serves at least one requested outcome and remove unmatched calls. For each remaining call, compare its arguments field by field with that endpoint's schema and the request: use exact parameter names and declared types, place each parameter exactly once in the required or optional bucket specified by the schema, and include each compatible explicit constraint in its accepted form. When supported, preserve both bounds of a range rather than using an exact-value field. Omit unsupported or unrequested values, and do not fabricate missing required values. Emit one call object per endpoint invocation. Finally, validate the complete response as valid JSON in the exact active format and wrapper, with exact tool names, allowed keys, required empty arrays, and well-formed parameter objects; check for duplicate keys, malformed wrappers, bundled calls, or extra text.
